2_Introduction: Within a framework of controlled experimental inputs, a perovskite cell configuration was fabricated, ultimately manifesting a PCE of 19.4%, FF of 73.62%, Voc of 1.1038 V, and Jsc of 23.87 mA/cm². The perovskite (Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1) precursor solution was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L in a mixed solvent of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrate at 1000 rpm for 15 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. An antisolvent injection of 180 µL at last 10 s stabilized the intermediate phase, leading to enhanced film quality. The film was then annealed at 105 °C for 30 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at 4.00°, with an intensity of 71.75 cts，which corresponds to the formation of a 2D structure within the perovskite lattice. The high intensity implies efficient surface passivation, contributing positively to device performance. GIXRD analysis further revealed a residual tensile stress of 10.50 MPa in the perovskite film via measurement conducted at an incident angle of 1°.
3_Result_Discussion: The fabrication of the Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 perovskite film employed a high-concentration precursor solution and a two-step spin-coating process, where the optimized antisolvent injection timing and volume during the final seconds of deposition rapidly triggered nucleation from the DMSO-coordinated intermediate phase, while the subsequent thermal annealing at 105°C promoted Ostwald ripening for dense, pinhole-minimized morphology critical for charge transport. This crystallization control was structurally corroborated by XRD analysis, which identified a distinct low-angle diffraction peak at 4.00° with significant intensity, signifying the in-situ formation of a low-dimensional perovskite phase that passivates surface and grain boundary defects through its insulating organic spacers, thereby suppressing non-radiative recombination. This structural passivation is further contextualized by GIXRD measurements revealing a residual tensile stress of 10.50 MPa within the lattice, a state which can influence ion migration kinetics and phase stability. The synergistic effect of the optimized crystallization dynamics and the embedded 2D passivating structure collectively enhanced interfacial charge extraction and bulk carrier lifetime, ultimately yielding a device with a VOC of 1.1038 V, a JSC of 23.87 mA/cm², an FF of 73.62%, and a PCE of 19.4%.
